name: Obsidian
tagline: Local-first Markdown note-taking with graph view and plugins
painPoints: Powerful but requires extensive plugin setup and maintenance
No proactive AI — only what community plugins add
Sync across devices costs extra as paid add-ons
Steep learning curve for graph-based knowledge management
Cannot manage email, calendar, or tasks natively
metaTitle: Obsidian Alternative in {{CURRENT_YEAR}}: Memory Without Plugins
metaDescription: Obsidian needs plugins and manual links. GAIA builds memory from your email and calendar and links ideas for you. Source-available and self-hostable.
whyPeopleLook: Obsidian's local-first, Markdown-based approach to knowledge management has built a devoted following. Its graph view, bidirectional linking, and plugin ecosystem are genuinely powerful for personal knowledge management (PKM). But Obsidian requires constant curation — you need to write, link, and tag everything manually. There is no AI that automatically captures meeting notes, creates links between related concepts, or proactively surfaces relevant past notes. Users who want the graph-based knowledge promise without the maintenance overhead increasingly look for AI-native alternatives.
gaiaReplaces: Graph-based memory that connects people, projects, and conversations automatically
Automatic meeting note capture from calendar events
Knowledge retrieval via semantic search without manual tagging
Context-aware information surfacing from past conversations and notes
gaiaAdvantages: Memory is built automatically: no manual note-taking required
Graph relationships are inferred by AI, not manually linked
Integrated with email and calendar so context is always complete
Proactive memory surfacing without needing to search manually
migrationSteps: Export your Obsidian vault as Markdown files
Ingest key notes into GAIA's memory system for semantic search
Continue using Obsidian for long-form writing and archiving if desired
Use GAIA for automatic capture of meeting notes and task-related context

faqs.question: Does GAIA have a graph view like Obsidian?
faqs.answer: GAIA uses a graph-based memory architecture internally but does not provide a visual graph view for browsing notes. Its strength is automatic knowledge capture and proactive retrieval, not manual knowledge visualization.

faqs.question: Is GAIA good for long-form writing like Obsidian?
faqs.answer: Obsidian is superior for long-form writing, Markdown formatting, and building a curated PKM vault. GAIA is better for automatic knowledge capture, cross-tool context, and proactive assistance.

faqs.question: Is GAIA source-available like Obsidian?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA is source-available (PolyForm Noncommercial). Unlike Obsidian (which has a closed core despite community plugins), GAIA's entire codebase is available on GitHub.

faqs.question: Does GAIA store notes locally like Obsidian?
faqs.answer: Self-hosted GAIA stores all data on your own servers, giving you similar local-first data control to Obsidian's local vault. GAIA Cloud stores data on GAIA's infrastructure with encryption.

comparisonRows.gaia: Memory that builds itself from email, calendar, and conversations, with actions attached to every recall
comparisonRows.competitor: Local-first Markdown editor and knowledge base for capturing, linking, and exploring personal notes and ideas

comparisonRows.gaia: Knowledge linked automatically across people, projects, and threads, with no manual graph to tend
comparisonRows.competitor: Best-in-class Markdown editor with bidirectional links, tags, graph view, canvas, and an extensive plugin ecosystem for building a personal knowledge base

comparisonRows.gaia: Email triaged, drafted, and automated in place, instead of copied into a vault by hand
comparisonRows.competitor: No email integration. Email content must be manually copied or routed into the vault; no triage, drafting, or automation

comparisonRows.gaia: Tasks captured from email and meetings with prioritization and reminders, beyond manual syntax and queries
comparisonRows.competitor: Supports task syntax in Markdown and community plugins like Tasks and Dataview for querying todos, but all capture and management is manual

comparisonRows.gaia: Proactive automation and cross-tool actions built in, not plugins you invoke for every step
comparisonRows.competitor: No built-in AI; community plugins provide LLM-powered features such as text generation and summarization, but require manual invocation for every action

comparisonRows.gaia: Scripted outcomes across external services from conversation, beyond templating inside the vault
comparisonRows.competitor: Templater and community plugins enable scripted note creation and some automation within the vault; no cross-tool or external service automation

comparisonRows.gaia: Every device in sync out of the box with self-hosting available, no add-on or DIY sync chains
comparisonRows.competitor: Obsidian Sync is a paid add-on for end-to-end encrypted sync; alternatively, users self-manage sync via iCloud, Dropbox, or Git

comparisonRows.gaia: Source-available and self-hostable like Obsidian, auditable end to end
comparisonRows.competitor: Core app is free but closed-source; local files are yours, but the application itself is proprietary and cannot be self-hosted or audited
